statements.impact_statement: Alias CVE-2025-69872. fastWorkflow uses diskcache only as DSPy's on-disk LM response cache (via dspy.configure_cache). Exploitation requires an attacker to write attacker-controlled pickle bytes into the process-local DSPy cache directory (default under the service account home, e.g. ~/.dspy_cache) and then have the process deserialize them. Remote API/MCP clients cannot write that directory. An adversary who can already write arbitrary files as the service user has equivalent or greater privilege than pickle RCE would grant. There is no patched diskcache release on PyPI as of this VEX; the finding remains accepted under this justification.
statements.status_notes: Code review 2026-08-08 (Dependabot alert #48); re-validated 2026-08-21 after v3.1.2 merge and datasets CVE-2026-66007 remediation. diskcache is transitive via dspy; not imported directly by fastworkflow. Cache path is not a multi-tenant shared volume in supported deployments. Re-evaluate if a deployment mounts the DSPy disk cache directory as world-writable or shares it across trust boundaries. Dual-stated as CVE-2025-69872 below for scanners that key on CVE IDs. PyPI latest remains 5.6.3 (no fixed release).

statements.impact_statement: Same assessment as GHSA-w8v5-vhqr-4h9v: DiskCache pickle RCE is not reachable by remote fastWorkflow clients; requires local write to the DSPy cache directory.
statements.status_notes: Paired statement so Trivy/OSV-keyed tools and Grype/GHSA-keyed tools both suppress Dependabot #48.

statements.impact_statement: Vulnerable component: authenticate_user in litellm/proxy/auth/login_utils.py. Affects litellm up to 1.82.2 only (OSV/NVD range); fastworkflow locks litellm 1.95.x and the scanned image carries 1.101.0, so the vulnerable code is not present. Independently, the affected code is in the litellm PROXY server (litellm/proxy/...), which fastworkflow never runs: it uses litellm only as a client via dspy.LM and litellm.completion and depends on plain litellm without the proxy extra.
statements.status_notes: Reviewed 2026-10-11 against a downstream workflow's 3.1.0-dev image scan (2026-09-22) and the fastworkflow 3.6.0 lock. Scanner match is a range false positive.

statements.impact_statement: Vulnerable component: Transformer-XL model-file deserialization (ZDI deserialization/code-injection batch; requires a user to load or convert a malicious checkpoint of that architecture). fastworkflow loads only BERT-family checkpoints with transformers (intent detection: google/bert_uncased_L-4_H-128_A-2 and distilbert-base-uncased, or operator-set INTENT_DETECTION_* models, plus models it trained itself; consistency: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 with local_files_only=True), never with trust_remote_code, and it never runs transformers' checkpoint conversion scripts. None of these model types or conversion scripts is reachable.
statements.status_notes: Reviewed 2026-10-11 against a downstream workflow's 3.1.0-dev image scan (2026-09-22) and the fastworkflow 3.6.0 lock. No patched release listed upstream; OSV ranges name 4.5x/5.0.0rc0 builds.

statements.impact_statement: Vulnerable component: pt2 loading handler (deserialization, local access). fastworkflow uses torch only for CPU inference/fine-tuning of its BERT-family intent models (CPU wheel from the pytorch-cpu index). It never loads .pt2/exported programs, never uses TorchScript or flatbuffer modules, has no CUDA/NCCL path in the CPU build, and neither it nor the BERT/DistilBERT modeling code it runs calls torch.nan_to_num.
statements.status_notes: Reviewed 2026-10-11 against a downstream workflow's 3.1.0-dev image scan (2026-09-22) and the fastworkflow 3.6.0 lock. No fixed torch release listed upstream.
